excerpts.content: Re 1, some reasons to not send the finalized header are extended non-finality periods where the `finalized_header` could be very old, in which case you want to leave it out to allow updating `next_sync_committee` (which is based on `finalized_header` if present). The protocol must still work even in those situations. Also, you may have clients using checkpoint sync that simply don't have access to a finalized header for historic data.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Exactly. Having a specific validator be part of the sync committee is a very rare occurrence, and due to the light client not being able to verify the current slashing status of signers, adding a new kind of slashing condition would not protect historic data where a rogue validator was already selected in the past. They can keep making signatures for those periods even when they have been slashed. So, the slashing would not primarily help the light client or network security in general; it is weaker than the existing attestation and proposer violations.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
`finalized_header` in `LightClientStore` is not the same concept as the regular `finalized_header`. 
It just means that the light client will not revert to data preceding it, i.e. that it now trusts the `next_sync_committee` and will no longer switch to a different one for that period.

The finalized header is not signed, it is included as a merkle proof.
`BeaconState` contains a field called `finalized_checkpoint` and that one has a `root` and `epoch`. The `root` is referring to the `finalized_header` that is included with the `LightClientUpdate`. The signature is always for `attested_header`.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Like, you hash the `finalized_header` to determine its block `root`, and then verify that this `root` is inside the `finalized_checkpoint.root` field of `attested_header` using `finality_proof`.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
The annotated spec is not up-to-date w.r.t. the latest spec additions. The fields have been renamed and the logic has become easier:
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.1.10/specs/altair/sync-protocol.md

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
In the old version, `finality_header` was indeed the one being signed (but this was not the finalized_header actually, but instead the attested header that contains the `header` as its `finality_proof` – so `header` would now be the `finalized_header`, and `finality_header` would be named `attested_header` now ). It was a confusing naming. If there was no `finality_header`, the one being signed was `header` itself.

In the new version, `attested_header` is the always the one being signed, and `finalized_header` is the finalized_header, if supplied.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
Non-finalized `LightClientUpdate`:
– Old spec: `header` / New spec: `attested_header` – `next_sync_committee` is rooted in this blockheader

Finalized `LightClientUpdate`:
– Old spec: `finality_header` / New spec: `attested_header`
– Old spec: `header` / New spec: `finalized_header` – `next_sync_committee` is rooted in this blockheader

excerpts.author: shresth
excerpts.content: <@!881905303011086387> thanks for the clarification! This really made things better for me. Can you explain what is the `finalized_header` in the new spec? I was assuming it is the last `finalised_header` in the beacon chain as per the Casper FFG?

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
As part of `LightClientUpdate`, it is the same as in Casper FFG (as in, it IS the same one referred to in the block's post-`BeaconState`'s `finalized_checkpoint.root`)
As part of `LightClientStore`, it just means that the light client considers it finalized and will not revert before it.

There are a couple conditions where the `LightClientStore`'s `finalized_header` may be updated irregularly:
– In period of extended non-finality spanning more than a sync committee period (~1 day), verifying the update would not be possible with just the `next_sync_committee`. An even later sync committee would be required to verify.
– When sync committee participation is low, there is not sufficient support to deem a `LightClientUpdate` safe.

In both of these situations, the light client is still expected to proceed / it must not become randomly stuck. The `best_update` may be applied as the next `finalized_header`, even when the light client could not determine safely that it was a finalized.

Both of the conditions are edge cases, so in normal operation, `finalized_header` is the same as for a full node.
In edge case, the `LightClientStore`'s `finalized_header` is a best-effort approximation of it.

excerpts.author: shresth
excerpts.content: <@!881905303011086387> I will re read the specs with those points in mind. Just confirming: in `LightClientUpdate` the `Finalized_Header` is always present as the last finalised block is always defined?

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
– If `LightClientUpdate` includes a non-zero `finalized_header`, it always corresponds to the `finaliezd_checkpoint.root` at the time of `attested_header`'s post-state.
– It may still be omitted for two reasons:
   – The `finalized_header` is very old. In this case, including it would require knowledge of a far future `next_sync_committee` which the light client cannot access, to validate the `attested_header`. In this case it makes sense to omit the `finalized_header` as a server so the light client can at least follow along with `next_sync_committee` (which is rooted in `attested_header` if no `finalized_header` is included).
   – The server does not have access to the `finalized_header` or its `finality_proof` for some reason. Examples:
      –  `finalized_header` could be missing because the server is not in sync (checkpoint sync, doing backfill)
      – `finality_proof` could be unavailable because it may require rewinding to old state to compute the proof, which is a costly operation that server may not be willing to do.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Updates without `finalized_header` are still useful, as a fallback for a delayed update using the `best_update` mechanism, and to update the `optimistic_header` in `LightClientStore`.
